correctness.rationale: For r>=2 and admissible positive path lengths, the potential z has edge gaps >=1, with equality at precisely the asserted contacts. Explicit nonnegative multipliers lambda_{i,j} produce its incidence divergence z and have total N; complementarity gives ||z||^2=N, and c=z/N belongs to the convex hull. Every root has norm squared 2, hence ||root-c||^2 <= 2-1/N. The weighted mean-square-distance identity 2-1/N+||y-c||^2 proves global optimality and unique center among all ambient centers. It also proves exact clearance for short terminal roots, counts all contacts, handles the direct edge, and establishes length-two-path invariance. Actual standalone exact-rational checks passed for 1,360 graphs, 18,925 roots, and 252 path-addition cases; finite verification does not replace this proof.

For unequal lengths there is no rank function whose increment is identically one on every arrow and whose value drops by the same source-to-sink amount on all paths: summing increments along two paths would force their lengths equal.

originality.rationale: A complete all-mixed-paths metric formula and exact contact screening were not found in the primary directed-edge/graph-root literature or the relevant published oriented-cycle published-finding corpus research record. The standard equal-norm convex duality, the graded equal-length subfamily, and distinct orientation-swapped path/cycle examples are explicitly acknowledged as covered prior principles or disjoint examples. The precise implication comparisons are recorded in the four checks below; an equivalent theorem under other network-optimization terminology remains a genuine residual risk.
residual_risks: Other equivalent formulations may occur under network embeddings, minimax edge potentials, isotonic regression, theta-digraph circumspheres, or optimal design, even if title/phrase searches do not retrieve them.
The general convex minball duality and covered semibalanced equal-length specialization are not discoveries in this report; these do not by themselves imply the claimed mixed-length contact formula.
A source search, even including primary full-text relevant sections, does not certify absence from all mathematical literature or unpublished results; independent priority review has not occurred.

value.rationale: The theorem completely evaluates a natural high-dimensional geometry invariant on arbitrary internally disjoint directed parallel-path networks, including full center coordinates, all root contacts, exact positive clearance margins, and an unexpected stability law under the canonical operation of attaching short paths. These structural consequences are parameter-uniform, sensitive to unequal path lengths, and useful as benchmarks for graph root polytopes and min-norm potential methods. They are neither a textbook one-line special case nor an arbitrary isolated finite instance.
